AssignGeneral.description: Send one of your generals to take command in another of your provinces.
AssignGeneral.title: AssignGeneral

Attack.description:
Attack an adjacent province owned by a nation you are at war with, or an independent one.

If you win, your surviving regiments take the province. Behind walls they lay a siege
instead: they camp before the walls, which fall once the siege reaches 100% (see
`siege_modifiers` on the province). Attacking a province you besiege sends reinforcements
to the siege lines; attacking a province of yours (or an ally's) under siege fights the
besiegers to relieve it.

A landing: from a coastal province, attack any province on the same sea zone where your
fleet is stronger than the defender's; the ships there carry the men (rules.ships carries)
and the defenders fight rules.sea_crossing_bonus + rules.landing_bonus harder on the beach.

general.description: Id of one of your generals in `origin` to lead them.
general.title: General

tactic.description: How to fight it, against the garrison's posture (see the province's `posture`). assault (carried by infantry) beats a garrison that skirmishes and breaks on one that holds the line; flank (cavalry; gains half as much in forest, hills, marsh and mountains) turns a held line and is caught by a sally; bombard (artillery) shatters a sally and is picked off by skirmishers. Worth rules.tactic_edge either way, as far as the regiments that carry it can; a tactic your army cannot carry (a flank without horse) costs as much as one outguessed. `targets` tells the best one.

units.description: Exactly which regiments attack, by kind, adding up to `regiments`. Leave out to send a proportional mix. Cavalry charges best on plains; every tenth of the army in artillery knocks a fort level off.
units.title: Units

Attack.title: Attack

BoostStability.description: Spend ducats to raise your stability by 1 (stability boosts ducat income).
BoostStability.title: BoostStability

Build.description:
Construct a building in one of your provinces. Each costs and does what the rules'
`buildings` catalogue says. A province has as many slots as its town allows (its
`building_slots` in the view), holds each building once, and a citadel needs a fort first.
Build.title: Build

BuildColonialFort.description:
Raise a fort over your colonies in a region (rules.colonial_fort_cost a level, up to
rules.colonial_fort_max): their defenders hold out rules.colonial_fort_defence better a
level.
BuildColonialFort.title: BuildColonialFort

BuildShips.description:
Launch ships from a port of yours into one of the sea zones it looks onto (name it if it
has more than one; see the province's `seas`). Galleys are cheap and rule calm seas;
galleons cost more, rule the ocean and carry more men (see rules.ships). A port launches
at most rules.ships_per_port ships a year, and one more for every 3 development.
BuildShips.title: BuildShips

Buy.description:
Buy from the European market at today's price plus the merchants' cut (see
`market`). What all Europe buys and sells this year moves next year's prices.
Buy.title: Buy

CancelTreaty.description:
End an alliance, a non-aggression pact, a marriage or every coalition with `target`
openly. No stability cost.
CancelTreaty.title: CancelTreaty

ChooseAgenda.description:
Give the reign an ambition, one of the agendas offered in your view (`agenda_offers`).
Fulfilled, it brings rules.agenda_prestige prestige and rules.agenda_authority authority,
and the ruler may take another.
ChooseAgenda.title: ChooseAgenda

ChooseOption.description:
Answer one of your pending events (see `me.pending_events`) with one of its options, by
index. Unanswered by the end of the next year, an event takes its first option.
ChooseOption.title: ChooseOption

ColonyKind.description: How a colony is founded and worked.
ColonyKind.title: ColonyKind

ConquerNatives.description:
March on the peoples of a region where you hold a colony: your garrison there and
`regiments` carried from your `port` against their strength on their own ground. Each
victory kills many of their warriors and brings plunder (and a little infamy); break them
and the plunder of an empire is yours, and they no longer deny anyone the region's dues.
ConquerNatives.title: ConquerNatives

Convert.description:
Send preachers to one of your provinces whose people keep another faith: it takes yours at
once, ending its discontent (a province of another faith yields rules.faith_mismatch_output
less). Costs rules.convert_cost plus convert_cost_per_development ducats a level; one a year.
Convert.title: Convert

DeclareWar.description:
Declare war. Breaks any alliance, non-aggression pact or truce with the target, which costs
stability and is seen by everyone. The target's allies are called to arms against you.
DeclareWar.title: DeclareWar

Develop.description: Invest ducats to raise a province's development by 1 (more output, more score).
Develop.title: Develop

Disband.description:
Send regiments home: they stop costing grain and ducats, and their men return to the
manpower pool (up to its cap).

unit.description: Only this kind; leave out for a proportional mix.

Disband.title: Disband

DismissAdvisor.description: Send an advisor away: no more salary, no more bonus.
DismissAdvisor.title: DismissAdvisor

EducateHeir.description:
Give the heir tutors in one of the three arts of rule: +1 to that skill (up to 6), for
rules.education_cost and rules.education_authority authority. Once a year.
EducateHeir.title: EducateHeir

Focus.description:
What a province's people turn their hands to. A focus strengthens one side of its
output, the more the larger its town.
Focus.title: Focus

FoundViceroyalty.description:
Make a region where you hold rules.viceroyalty_colonies colonies a viceroyalty, under a
viceroy of skill 1 to 3: more cargo there (rules.viceroy_cargo a point of skill), and the
colonies better held. Costs rules.viceroyalty_cost and rules.viceroyalty_authority.
FoundViceroyalty.title: FoundViceroyalty

Gift.description: Give resources to another nation, no strings attached.
Gift.title: Gift

HireAdvisor.description:
Bring one of the candidates at your court onto your council (see
`advisor_candidates` in your view). Replaces whoever holds that seat.
HireAdvisor.title: HireAdvisor

HireGeneral.description: Appoint a new general in one of your provinces. His skill (1 to 3) is up to fortune.
HireGeneral.title: HireGeneral

HireMercenaries.description:
Hire mercenary pikemen (Landsknechte, Swiss) in one of your provinces for ducats alone:
no manpower and no iron, at the rules' mercenary_cost a regiment, up to mercenary_limit
regiments a year. Once hired they serve, eat and are paid like any infantry.
HireMercenaries.title: HireMercenaries

Improve.description:
Improve the workings of one of your provinces by a level (up to 3): its mine,
vineyard, fishery or looms, by what it is known for. Each level adds half of what its good
yields; it takes no building slot. The next level costs the rules' improve_cost times it.
Improve.title: Improve

LiftSiege.description: Raise a siege you lay: the besiegers march back to one of your provinces next to it.
LiftSiege.title: LiftSiege

Move.description:
Move regiments between two adjacent provinces that you own. Happens before battles. By
sea too: between two of your coastal provinces on the same sea zone, if your ships there
can carry them and no enemy fleet commands it.

general.description: Id of one of your generals in `origin` to lead them.
general.title: General

units.description: Exactly which regiments go, by kind, adding up to `regiments`. Leave out to send a proportional mix of what stands in `origin`.
units.title: Units

Move.title: Move

Patronize.description:
Patronise painters, churches and feasts: once a year, spend patronage_base ducats plus
patronage_per_prestige for every point of prestige you hold, for patronage_prestige more
prestige. Prestige raises income and counts in the final score.
Patronize.title: Patronize

PolicyAxis.description: A great choice of how the realm is run: one side or the other, or neither.
PolicyAxis.title: PolicyAxis

Posture.description: How a province's garrison waits for an attack.
Posture.title: Posture

PressClaim.description:
A throne's line has failed and your crown, married into it, holds a claim (see `claims`
in your view): press it by war, or renounce it for the goodwill of its court. The claim is
spent either way.
PressClaim.title: PressClaim

Proclaim.description:
Speak to all Europe: a public proclamation every court reads next turn. Like letters, it
binds nobody.
Proclaim.title: Proclaim

ProposeAlliance.description: Offer an alliance. Allies share vision and are called to arms when one is attacked.
ProposeAlliance.title: ProposeAlliance

ProposeCoalition.description:
Invite `target` into a defensive league against `against`, a power whose infamy has
reached rules.coalition_infamy. Once signed, if `against` declares war on either of you, the
other (and every other court leagued against it) goes to war at once, without being asked.
The league dissolves when the conqueror's infamy falls below rules.coalition_dissolves.
ProposeCoalition.title: ProposeCoalition

ProposeMarriage.description:
Offer a royal marriage between the two houses. It lasts until war breaks it: both courts
warm to each other by rules.opinion_marriage_yearly every year. At most rules.max_marriages
for a realm.
ProposeMarriage.title: ProposeMarriage

ProposeNonAggression.description: Offer a non-aggression pact for a fixed number of turns.
ProposeNonAggression.title: ProposeNonAggression

ProposePeace.description:
Offer peace to a nation you are at war with. Accepted peace starts a five-year truce and
carries out the terms. The recipient may accept, reject, or answer with a counter-offer.

ask_tribute.description: Ducats a year they pay you, for 10 years.
ask_tribute.title: Ask Tribute

limit_army.description: Their army may not grow beyond this many regiments while the truce lasts.
limit_army.title: Limit Army

note.description: Your words to go with the offer: arguments, threats, promises. They bind nobody.
note.title: Note

pay_tribute.description: Ducats a year you pay them, for 10 years.
pay_tribute.title: Pay Tribute

ProposePeace.title: ProposePeace

ProposeTrade.description:
Offer an exchange: you give `give` and receive `receive` if the target accepts.

Asking for something while giving nothing is a demand for tribute.

note.description: Your words to go with the offer: arguments, threats, promises. They bind nobody.
note.title: Note

ProposeTrade.title: ProposeTrade

Recruit.description:
Raise new regiments of one kind in one of your provinces. Pikemen (infantry) can be
raised anywhere; cavalry needs stables in the province and artillery a cannon foundry. See
`rules.units` for what each kind costs and how it fights.
Recruit.title: Recruit

Region.description:
The lands beyond the sea that crowns may colonise: not on the map, but in the menu of
the New World.
Region.title: Region

RequestCallToArms.description:
Ask an ally to join your war against `enemy`. An ally who refuses or ignores the call
dissolves the alliance, in public.
RequestCallToArms.title: RequestCallToArms

Research.description:
Advance one technology branch by a level: military (stronger armies), economy (richer
provinces), engineering (cheaper building and development), naval (stronger fleets, cheaper
ships, faster expeditions) or administration (a steadier realm, cheaper research, less
infamy). One research a year. Some levels need a level of another branch first (see
rules.tech_tree requires). Every level offers doctrines to choose between: `choice` is the
index of the one you take, for good.
Research.title: Research

Resources.description: A bundle of the six national resources. Never negative.
Resources.title: Resources

Respond.description:
Accept or reject a proposal addressed to you. Unanswered proposals expire; ignoring a call
to arms from an ally dissolves the alliance.

To haggle over a peace or a trade, reject it with a `counter`: your own terms, written from
your side (`give` is what you would pay). It reaches them as a new proposal next turn, and
they can accept, reject or counter again. A trade's counter may only use `give`, `receive`
and `note`.
Respond.title: Respond

RoyalAct.description: What a crown can do by its own authority (see Rules.royal_acts).
RoyalAct.title: RoyalAct

RoyalAction.description:
Spend the crown's authority (it gathers every year by the ruler's skills) on a royal
act (see rules.royal_acts for each one's cost and effect): an extraordinary levy, a royal
progress, calling the banners, a general pardon, a royal embassy to `target`, leading the
army in person, or patronage of the Church.

target.description: The court an embassy goes to.

RoyalAction.title: RoyalAction

SailFleet.description:
Sail ships from a sea zone to a neighbouring one, before the battles: fleets move a zone
a year, as armies march a province. Sail into an enemy's zone and seek_battle there the
same year.
SailFleet.title: SailFleet

ScrapShips.description: Lay up ships of yours in a sea zone.
ScrapShips.title: ScrapShips

SeekBattle.description:
Send your fleet in a sea zone against the fleet of a realm you are at war with in the
same zone, after the fleets have sailed and before the armies march. Strength is each
ship's in that kind of water, times a roll of the dice and each realm's morale; the beaten
fleet loses half its ships. A fleet rules.fleet_command times the enemy's in a zone closes
its straits to the enemy's armies and blockades its ports there; any fleet stronger than
the defender's lets your armies cross its straits freely and land on its shores.
SeekBattle.title: SeekBattle

SeizeColony.description:
At war, take one of an enemy's colonies in a region. Colonies nobody defends fall to a
fleet: your Atlantic fleet must be rules.seize_command times the enemy's (England's Sea Dogs
need less). Colonies held by a garrison or by settlers must be stormed: `regiments` sail
from your `port` (and your own garrison in the region joins them), your ocean fleet at least
the enemy's; they fight the defenders behind their forts. Win, and the colony is yours and
the survivors garrison it; lose, and they come back to the port.
SeizeColony.title: SeizeColony

Sell.description: Sell to the European market at today's price minus the merchants' cut.
Sell.title: Sell

SendExpedition.description:
Send settlers and soldiers to found a colony in a region beyond the sea (see
`new_world` in your view: what each region yields, when it opens, how many places are left
and how fast your expeditions go). Needs a port of yours on the Atlantic or the Baltic and
an escort of rules.expedition_ships fleet strength there; costs rules.expedition_cost, times
the kind's cost (rules.colony_kinds). Each year it makes progress; at 100% the colony is
founded, unless the region filled up first. A plantation ships the region's full cargo and
angers its peoples; a trading post is cheap and quick but ships 60%; a settlement starts at
half, grows to half again as much, and defends itself.
SendExpedition.title: SendExpedition

SendMessage.description:
Send a private diplomatic message. The target reads it next turn. It has no effect on
the rules: words are only words.
SendMessage.title: SendMessage

SetFocus.description:
Turn one of your provinces to a focus: trade (more ducats), farming (more grain), mining
(more iron and timber), garrison (more manpower, defended harder) or learning (cheaper to
develop; each province of learning makes the realm's research cheaper). The bonus is
rules.focus_base plus focus_per_settlement for each step its town has grown above a hamlet.
Costs rules.focus_cost; a province keeps its focus at least rules.focus_years years.
SetFocus.title: SetFocus

SetPolicy.description:
Take a side on one of the realm's great choices (see rules.policies): army (a
professional army or militia levies), economy (agrarian or mercantile) or state (centralism
or fueros). The first side taken on an axis is free; changing it later costs
rules.policy_stability stability, and a policy stands at least rules.policy_years years.
SetPolicy.title: SetPolicy

SetPosture.description:
Tell the garrison of one of your provinces how to wait for an attack: hold (the line of
pikes, carried by infantry), skirmish (shot and bows thrown forward, carried by archers) or
sally (horse kept back to charge, carried by cavalry). Each beats one attacking tactic and
loses to another (see Attack.tactic). Free; whoever can see the garrison sees its posture.
SetPosture.title: SetPosture

SetStance.description:
Declare a court your friend or your rival, or neutral again. Stances are public: every
court sees them. A friend warms to you every year, a rival cools, and your regiments fight 5%
harder against a declared rival. At most three friends and three rivals.
SetStance.title: SetStance

SetTaxes.description:
Set the realm's taxes from -2 (very low) to +2 (very high). Each level up brings
rules.tax_income_step more ducat income and rules.tax_manpower_step less manpower, makes
raising stability dearer, and above 0 risks a point of stability every year; below 0 the
people may grow content and stability rise. The level stays until changed.
SetTaxes.title: SetTaxes

ShipTroops.description:
Carry regiments from one of your ports on the ocean or the Baltic to garrison your
colonies in a region (rules.garrison_pay ducats a year each; they calm the peoples and hold
the colonies against a storm), or with `home` bring them back to the port. Your ships on the
ocean must carry them, and no enemy fleet command the ocean.
ShipTroops.title: ShipTroops

Stance.description: A court's declared attitude towards another, public to all Europe.
Stance.title: Stance

Tactic.description:
How an attack is fought. Each wins against one posture and loses against another, and
is only as good as the regiments that carry it.
Tactic.title: Tactic

TakeDecision.description:
Take one of your crown's national decisions (`decisions` in your view), once its goals
hold and you can pay its authority and ducats: it pays at once and leaves a lasting effect,
and some give the realm a new name. Each is taken once.
TakeDecision.title: TakeDecision

Terms.description:
What a peace (or a counter-offer) settles. Everything is optional: no terms at all is a
white peace. Lump sums are capped by what the payer has; provinces must belong to the side
that hands them over, cannot be a capital, and must border the realm that receives them (or
another province it receives in the same peace).

ask_tribute.description: Ducats a year they pay you, for 10 years.
ask_tribute.title: Ask Tribute

limit_army.description: Their army may not grow beyond this many regiments while the truce lasts.
limit_army.title: Limit Army

note.description: Your words to go with the offer: arguments, threats, promises. They bind nobody.
note.title: Note

pay_tribute.description: Ducats a year you pay them, for 10 years.
pay_tribute.title: Pay Tribute

Terms.title: Terms

UpgradeBuilding.description:
Raise a building standing in one of your provinces to its next level: it does more (and
eats more), by `rules.building_level_factors`, up to its `max_level`. It costs its own
cost times `rules.building_upgrade_costs` for the new level. Once a year per building.
UpgradeBuilding.title: UpgradeBuilding

UpgradeMonument.description:
Raise the monument of one of your provinces by a level (from a bare site to level 1, up
to `rules.max_monument_level`). Its bonus grows with every level and serves whoever holds
it.
UpgradeMonument.title: UpgradeMonument

description: Everything a nation wants to do this turn, in the order it wants it done.

counsel.description: What each advisor counselled this year, by seat. Private, like `thoughts`.
counsel.title: Counsel

thoughts.description: The ruler's private reasoning this year. No other court sees it; it is kept in the record, for the chronicle of the game.
thoughts.title: Thoughts

title: Orders
